FINDING 1, the efficiency answer, already proven this pass: one rg pipeline returns the complete OPEN set in 82ms with no paging and no line bodies, namely rg -o --no-filename with the capture-only pattern anchored to tolerate a leading double pipe; the ledger is a single table whose note lines run to thousands of characters, so every tool that reads whole lines pays for prose it does not need, and a naive leading-pipe anchor silently misses the very rows the census exists to find. This yields 25 OPEN IDs. FINDING 2, and the reason a regex alone is not the fix, a CORRECTNESS bug rather than a speed one: the same transcript concluded that the opencode (me-so-poor) heartbeat claims B5-0572, B5-0573, B5-0574 and B5-0577, but that heartbeat records live_claims as an empty list and current_task as null, and this seeder holds no claim; those four IDs appear only inside the narrative last_completed prose string. A reader that greps a JSON blob for task IDs manufactures a claim set out of English. Making the query faster over a worse data model would only deliver a wrong answer sooner, so B5-0609 seeds a read-only query tool that owns the join and parses structured fields only, never prose. An absent signal must be UNKNOWN, never live. QUEUE 0628 (2026-09-27, opencode (space-bunny-free), from the human's own failed hermes run rather than from a seeded row): the runner was unusable with any subcommand-style agent CLI, and the human's terminal output supplied the evidence. `hermes` rejected the tail of the task prompt with "is not a `hermes` command" and exited 2, and the fragment it quoted began immediately after the phrase "Reusable lesson" in the template, which located the cause before anything was guessed. Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not escape embedded double quotes when handing an argument to a native executable: the quotes act as argument delimiters, so the prompt is split into several argv entries, the first fragment is consumed as the prompt and the remainder are read as positional arguments, and a subcommand-style CLI reports the last of them as an invalid command. Confirmed by controlled reproduction rather than inference, with four cases run against hermes itself: a two-line prompt with newlines exited 0 and was understood, proving newlines are safe and are NOT the trigger; the same prompt with its double quotes removed exited 0 and executed; the same prompt retaining its double quotes exited 2 with the exact error the human saw; and a native argv dumper under python.exe, which receives arguments through the identical Windows marshalling path, reported ARGC=2 for a quoted prompt and ARGC=1 for the identical prompt with quotes neutralised. The fix is the minimal one the evidence supports, namely neutralise double quotes in the prompt immediately before invocation and change nothing else, so the multi-line structure the agent reads is preserved; newlines were deliberately left intact because they were tested and are harmless. Verified end to end by running the real runner against the native dumper, which received the prompt as exactly ONE argument of 1007 characters with 12 newlines preserved, no double quote present, and the task id correctly substituted. DISCLOSED SIDE EFFECT: while isolating the trigger, a live probe prompt was sent to hermes that instructed it to write a reusable-lesson file, and hermes complied, creating `.agent/PATTERNS/solar-pro4<U+2028>free/lesson-compile-gate-grep.md` in solar-pro4's namespace, which is a namespace this agent may read but must never write. The file was confirmed to be this session's own creation by its 04:24:28Z creation time against a 02:34Z session start, read to confirm its contents, then deleted, leaving the eight pre-existing files in that namespace untouched. The lesson from that misstep is recorded rather than glossed: a reproduction that runs against a live tool must use a prompt that cannot cause a write, because the tool will do exactly what it is told.

QUEUE 0649 (2026-09-27, opencode (space-bunny-free), on human approval to stop the two shipped census tools disagreeing about the same claim): this row exists because a live hermes run on B5-0631 made the disagreement observable rather than theoretical. That run wrote its claim with `started_utc` of `2026-09-27T00:00:00Z`, a placeholder rather than the real time, so the claim's own age read 292 minutes against a 30-minute TTL. `ledger-query.ps1` correctly called the claim LIVE, because it takes the newest of the claim and the owner heartbeat and the heartbeat was 12 minutes old. `run-queue.ps1` read `started_utc` ALONE, so it would have declared the claim abandoned and handed a task held by a working agent to a second claimant, which is the duplicate-delivery failure the whole claims protocol exists to prevent. The B5-0597 lesson had already been written, and had already been implemented in one tool, and the second tool simply never received it, so the lesson existed as prose and as a working implementation in one place and as the opposite behaviour in the other. `Test-LiveClaim` is now aligned onto the two-signal rule, and the punctuation-normalised `Get-NormName` is copied VERBATIM from `ledger-query.ps1` rather than reimplemented, because a second hand-rolled variant is how the two came to disagree. One divergence is deliberate and documented in the function: `ledger-query` reports UNKNOWN when no heartbeat matches the owner, being a reporting tool that can print a verdict, whereas the runner's question is binary, so an owner who never wrote a heartbeat at all falls back to the claim's own age, because returning not-live there would let one heartbeat-less claim block its task forever, a worse failure than the one being fixed; when nothing at all can be determined the task is still not offered. Verified against the live case first, where the runner now declines B5-0631 and offers B5-0633 instead, and then against seven synthetic cases in an isolated temp harness, all PASS, being a 9-hour claim with no heartbeat falling back to FREE, the hermes case of a 9-hour claim plus a 2-minute heartbeat reading TAKEN, a 9-hour claim plus an 8-hour heartbeat reading FREE, a fresh claim with no heartbeat reading TAKEN, a corrupt claim file never being stolen, no claim file reading FREE, and a future-dated claim treated as live for clock skew. The first synthetic run was itself defective and was discarded rather than believed, because the harness had a typo in the timestamp format string which made every timestamp unparseable so all cases silently fell back to claim-file mtime and reported a uniform wrong answer, and because a U+2028 separator had been typed as literal placeholder text; the harness was corrected and a sanity assertion added that the generated timestamp actually parses, which is the check whose absence let the broken harness look authoritative.

FINDING 1, and it is the reason this wave is worth more than the governance waves before it. Rulebook :178 states that during the Shadow War no player may achieve a Standard Victory, B5-0354 recorded that guard as a hard prerequisite to be in place from day one, and B5-0375 closed its task by asserting that Shadow War suppression covers both conditions. Neither statement survives contact with the code. RulesEngine.java carries exactly ONE isShadowWar test in the whole engine, at line 618 inside stationVictory, which is Standard Victory condition 2. The condition 1 path, the per-player scan at lines 583 to 601 and its standardVictory helper at lines 641 to 644, has no guard at all, so a player with 20 or more power who is strictly leading still crowns a Standard Victory during a Shadow War. The suite repeats the error in prose: the VIC section javadoc at HeadlessConformanceTest.java line 1872 says check 7 asserts that Shadow War suppresses condition 1 and condition 2, but check 7 at lines 1947 to 1951 exercises only condition 2 with a 15 power leader, so the condition-1 half of that sentence was never asserted and is false. This is the repo's own filed lesson arriving in a new costume, a document asserting a property the code does not have.

FINDING 2, from the same read. Rulebook :180 to :183 defines Major Victory as at least 20 Power and at least 10 more than each other player, and a case-insensitive search for "major victory" across b5ccg/src, docs and .agent/REPORTS returns ZERO occurrences. The path does not exist. This is the B5-0594 audit gap 3, left open, and it is not theoretical: premiere.json carries real major agendas, isMajorAgenda true appears in the card data, and RulesEngine.java line 598 bars exactly those players from the Standard path, so any player holding a Major Agenda whose own condition is unmet currently has no power-based way to win, and a game in which every survivor is in that state can only end by forfeit.

SECOND FINDING, RECORDED SO THE NEXT ATTEMPT IS NOT BUILT ON B5-0966 RECOMMENDATION 1: the report's prescribed cp1252 to utf-8 three-round repair DOES NOT REACH A FIXPOINT and silently leaves 1,358 of 1,504 mojibake marks behind, so anyone running it as written would file a partial repair that still looks damaged. Cause measured: the damage includes C1 control characters in the 0x80 to 0x9F range, which Python cp1252 refuses to encode, so 1,050 of the 1,081 marked lines raise UnicodeEncodeError on round one and only 124 lines change at all. THE PRESENCE TEST IS INSUFFICIENT AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY. Read B5-1415 plus B5-0755 first per the row. B5-1415 credited "in-file row labels" for making its 13-hunk 4-file engine triage need no style attribution; B5-0755 supplies the method rule adopted verbatim into the proposal, attribute on ADDED LINES ONLY, never anywhere in the diff, because context lines carry the old file's comments and will attribute new bytes to unrelated old tasks. MEASURED BEFORE PROPOSING, per-hunk over added lines only across the 7 dirty b5ccg slash src files at 45 hunks and 792 added lines: 33 of 45 hunks carry at least one row id (73 percent) AND 15 of 45 carry more than one (33 percent) with CardEffects dot java at 5 of 5, while 12 carry none (27 percent). So the convention B5-1415 relied on is real and widespread and this row does not start something nobody does, but a presence test would be GREEN on those 15 ambiguous hunks while the question it was meant to answer stays open, because the extra ids are citations (B5-0691 engine law, B5-0351 difficulty contract, B5-0669 card census) sharing the same explanatory comment that names the owner. B5-1415 got the right answer because an agent reasoned about which id was claiming and which were citing, and that reasoning is manual. THE RULE PROPOSED IS THEREFORE NOT add a label but add exactly one DISTINGUISHABLE label: the reserved token OWNER colon B5 dash NNNN, exactly one per hunk, on the line above the first added line or in a whole-new method's javadoc first line, naming the row the author worked rather than a row the code depends on, with citations keeping their current free form precisely because the reserved token makes them distinguishable by construction. The consuming triage procedure has five branches all mechanical (empty to UNLABELLED, more than one to CONFLICT, else attributed plus a status confirmation) so the only judgement left is reached by absence or multiplicity, never by reading prose and guessing. THREE DECISIONS WITH THEIR REASONS, each foreclosing the obvious cheap version: a label is a CLAIM not proof (the procedure confirms the row exists and reads its status, never concludes the work was done, which preserves B5-1415's sharpest observation that B5-1047's work product sits in the tree while its row reads OPEN instead of hiding it behind a green check); NO GATE is proposed (a comment convention is unenforceable, a stale marker is worse than a missing one because it is believed, and a rule that only ever produces a finding trains the fleet to ignore findings, so the convention is adopted and the gate declined because its entire value is in the 15 ambiguous and 12 unlabelled hunks); RETAGGING is permitted since the marker is commentary and git diff remains the arbiter, which makes adoption incremental at 33 hunks tagged with no code change. Not done deliberately: no edit to AGENTS dot md or guidelines slash Guidelines dot md, since per 00_BOOT step 4 a proposal is never truth until merged and adoption is a human adjudication; no src retagging pass, named in the proposal as a later separately-claimed task; no ledger row touched but B5-1465's own; no commit, no push. Reusable lesson: a convention measured only by presence passes on the cases it was meant to catch, so measure the property you need (one owner, distinguishable from a citation) not the one that is easy to count. ROW PREMISE CONFIRMED, NOT ALREADY DONE: there was no forfeit path at all. Player.setHasForfeited existed and checkVictory plus the station and tiebreak win conditions all honoured hasForfeited, but nothing could set it by choice -- GameAction.Type had no FORFEIT member and grep for forfeit across b5ccg/src found only setHasForfeited in Player.java plus four test fixtures, so every existing hasForfeited reader was reachable only from the involuntary draw-deck path in Player.drawCards (rulebook :460). LANDED: GameAction.Type.FORFEIT plus a GameAction.forfeit() factory (no card, no target -- forfeiting is a self-declared loss with nothing to aim at); RulesEngine.canForfeit gating on phase ACTION, game not over, state.isPlayerActive, and at least one other active player; RulesEngine.executeForfeit marking forfeited, discarding the ambassador, and returning checkVictory's winner only when the forfeit actually left a sole survivor; GameController processAction case FORFEIT. THE ROW'S THREE REQUIREMENTS, and how each is met. ACTION-phase-only: canForfeit returns false for DRAW, END_ROUND and SETUP, which keeps it disjoint from SURRENDER (canSurrender gates on DRAW, B5-0661) and from the involuntary draw-deck forfeit. Immediate loss: the controller sets the winner and RETURNS from processAction inside the branch rather than falling through to the end-of-action checkVictory at GameController.java:167, because that check runs only after the turn advances and one more action would have been processed for a player who had already lost. Victory to the opponent: reuses checkVictory rather than reimplementing it, so the forfeit path cannot disagree with the existing victory authority. A WORTH RECORDING SCOPE CALL: the row says victory goes to the opponent, which is only true in a two-player game. In three or more the forfeit removes one player and play continues -- executeForfeit awards nothing, because awarding there would hand the win to every remaining player and end a game the row does not say is over. That is why canForfeit also refuses when no other active player remains. FORFEIT IS NOT SURRENDER: surrender leaves the player out of play with the ambassador surviving and an asylum copy going to the winner (rulebook :819), whereas forfeit discards the ambassador; the two flags stay separate and a surrendered player cannot forfeit (FRT-R). The first text of this row said Make GameState.advanceRound clear the sustained-action registry and cited B5-2205 F1. That guidance is WITHDRAWN as a rulebook regression. Four independent sources say sustained actions PERSIST across rounds while the source stays rotated: rulebook :358, GameState.java:35-37 in code comments, the SUS test block headed 2 sustained action survives round boundary, and a probe measuring isSustaining still true after startRound. Following the original text would have contradicted the rulebook and would NOT have fixed any of the five failures, because not one of them was caused by the registry surviving. THE SEEDER OF THIS ROW CORRECTED IT AND RECORDED THE CORRECTION IN THE ROW ITSELF rather than quietly fixing the code to match bad guidance. THREE DISTINCT CAUSES, ALL MEASURED WITH A THROWAWAY PROBE COMPILED AGAINST THE TREE IN TEMP, NOT INFERRED FROM THE FAILURE NAMES. (1) REAL PRODUCT BUG, two symptoms AST and ROT: the ambassador assistant bonus was never cleared at the round boundary. RulesEngine.startRound unrotated the ambassador but never called setAssistantBonus on it, and the flag lives on the ambassador rather than on the assistant, so unrotating the assistant left the plus one in place. Probe: after executeAssistantAbilityBoost the ambassador read assistantBonus=true dip=4, and after startRound it STILL read assistantBonus=true dip=4 with the assistant already unrotated. Rulebook :492 gives the bonus only while the assistant remains rotated, so a one-turn plus one was surviving the boundary and boosting Diplomacy, Intrigue and Leadership that nobody was paying for. FIX, two files: new GameState.hasSustainedActionTargeting(Card,SustainedActionType), needed because the registry is private and keyed by SOURCE id so the existing getSustainedAction and isSustaining can only answer questions about the card sustaining and never about the card receiving the bonus; and a clear in RulesEngine.startRound that runs UNLESS a live sustained ASSISTANT_BONUS action targets that ambassador, which rulebook :492 expressly permits. Identity not id is the comparison, so a caller holding the live card gets the same answer the sustaining path registered. (2) WRONG CONSTANTS, two symptoms: fleet military includes leader leadership asserted 5 where the measured value is 6, and fleet military reverts to base after ending asserted 2 where the measured value is 3. The suites own helpers build a base-3 frigate via fleetCard and a leadership-3 character via leaderCard, and rulebook :358 makes the boost ADDITIVE, increase the Military rating, so 3 plus 3 is 6 and the unled baseline is 3. Both old constants assumed a base-2 frigate the helper never constructs. This was failing on CORRECT product behaviour. Corroborated from outside this block: FLR asserts IC character leads a second fleet 3 plus 2 equals 5 and LEAD asserts leader Military flows into the effective fleet value 3 plus 5, both of which pass today and both of which encode the same additive rule. (3) WRONG CONTRACT, one symptom: round number advanced asserted getRoundNumber equals before plus 1 across rules.startRound, but startRound is a per-TURN reset and the counter belongs to GameController.java:68 which calls state.advanceRound once the round completes. HeadlessConformanceTest:3348 already asserts that contract in words, only after advanceRound not during. Probe measured the round staying at 1. FOUR CHECKS ADDED so the corrected semantics cannot drift again: sustained action is still registered after startRound, startRound does not advance the round counter, advanceRound advances the round counter, and a contrast pair inside the SUS block where an UNSUSTAINED assistant boost flags the ambassador and then does NOT survive the round boundary. The sustained half of that conditional was already covered by ambassador bonus persists after startRound, which previously passed for the wrong reason, namely that nothing ever cleared the flag, and which now passes because hasSustainedActionTargeting genuinely permits it. Both branches of the new conditional are therefore pinned. DELIBERATE NON-CHANGE, clearAllSustainedActions at GameState.java:407 still has zero callers and I left it that way, because rulebook :358 requires sustained actions to survive the round boundary and wiring it into advanceRound would break the rules. Its javadoc says called at game end while no game-end path calls it, which is a doc and implementation mismatch recorded here rather than fixed under this row. THE PAYMENT DEFECT MEASURED: rulebook :657 defines ONE Sponsor action covering Character, Enhancement, Group, Location and Fleet, but the engine had three paths that disagreed and none for three of the five types. Character went through RECRUIT_CHARACTER with correct doubling (:663) and correct assistant discount (:492) but NO Inner-Circle rotation check; Group through canSponsorGroup at listed cost with an absolute race gate; and Enhancement, Location and Fleet were reachable ONLY through PLAY_CARDs generic applyGenericCardPlay, which charges the bare listed cost with no race restriction and no rotation, so an other-race restricted enhancement or a hostile-race location or fleet could be brought into play for its listed price where :665 says only the player controlling that race may play such cards. THE TWO COST TERMS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE and conflating them is the trap: :663 makes a different-race CHARACTER dearer at DOUBLE, while :664 and :665 make a different-race card of any OTHER type ILLEGAL, an absolute refusal never a doubled price. One off-race multiplier cannot express both, so sponsorshipCost keeps them apart by card type and delegates to the already-correct sponsorCost and groupSponsorshipCost rather than re-deriving them. LANDED: GameAction.Type.SPONSOR_CARD plus a sponsorCard(card, leader) factory riding the existing leader/card field pair as PROMOTE_CHARACTER and LEAD_FLEET do; RulesEngine.sponsorshipCost, sponsorshipListedCost, hasReadySponsor, canSponsorCard and executeSponsorCard; and one GameController dispatch branch that stays a dispatch and does not re-derive the cost the way the RECRUIT_CHARACTER branch must for its discount bookkeeping. executeSponsorCard applies the cost BEFORE anything moves, and Player.applyInfluence already refuses without deducting when the pool is short, so a refusal leaves the hand, the pool and the rotation exactly as they were and the refund case cannot arise. NO Inner-Circle TERM ON SPONSORSHIP: :657 charges the listed cost while only :669 adds one influence per existing IC member for PROMOTION, so a sponsor cost carrying an IC term would overcharge every sponsorship; a conformance check asserts a 2-member Inner Circle does not move the sponsorship price. THE ASSISTANT DISCOUNT NOW REACHES NON-CHARACTER SPONSORSHIP: :492 scopes it to sponsoring a card rather than to characters, and it previously applied only on the character path. THE PROMOTION PATH WAS ALREADY CORRECT and was left alone: promotionCost never consults getSponsorDiscount, which is exactly what :669 requires, and that non-application is now asserted rather than merely true. SECOND REAL DEFECT FIXED, an audit-trail bug: executePromote charged cost then logged a SECOND promotionCost(p, ch) call AFTER recruitToInnerCircle had already grown innerCircle.size(), so the log reported cost+1, contradicting the amount charged by exactly the IC term that makes promotion cost what it does. The charge was always right and only the record was wrong, which is worse here because that line is the audit trail; the log now reports the charged cost and decomposes it as listed plus per-member.
